title: Article 310 — Tenure of office of persons serving the Union or a State

content.study:
Topic at a Glance
Article 310 of the Constitution of India is titled “Tenure of office of persons serving the Union or a State”. It forms an integral component of Services under the Union and the States (Articles 308–323), located within the “Services” cluster. Current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023.

Constitutional Text & Anatomy
(1) Except as expressly provided by this Constitution, every person who is a member of a defence service or of a civil service of the Union or of an all-India service or holds any post connected with defence or any civil post under the Union holds office during the pleasure of the President, and every person who is a member of a civil service of a State or holds any civil post under a State holds office during the pleasure of the Governor 3 [omitted of the State.

(2) Notwithstanding that a person holding a civil post under the Union or a State holds office during the pleasure of the President or, as the case may be, of the Governor 2 [omitted of the State, any contract under which a person, not being a member of a defence service or of an all-India service or of a civil service of the Union or a State, is appointed under this Constitution to hold such a post may, if the President or the Governor 42 [omitted , as the case may be, deems it a State specified in Part A or Part B of the First Schedule\
